chapter: His own groups, compositions and friends
title: Resuming; his own working groups after coming to IU in 1966
summary: After the break Baker explains he kept playing with Indianapolis musicians for a year or two after moving to Bloomington, then formed bass and cello groups and a string quartet.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: A few minutes ago, after we were talking about George Russell’s groups, you said you’d like to talk about your own groups, once we got to I. U., so why don’t we go there now?
After I took the job at Indiana University, one of the things I had to be concerned about was still to be able to have some kind of vehicle to play my own music.
And that was 1966 that you came to here [to Indiana University].

I came in 1966. For probably the first year or two years after I came here, I kept working the group that I had in Indianapolis. I had a group of musicians that I played with: Sonny Smith – that was his own group – but I was also playing with Mingo Jones and Earl Van Riper. Sheryl Shay was singing with us. Chuck Carter, Al Reeves, and a
host of the other players. Willis Kirk. So I continued to work primarily with Indianapolis musicians.
And mostly in Indianapolis? Or did you play all around the area?
